display.purpose: The page title, in bright ink. 22ch at most; a title that is a sentence is 0.72 of this, 30ch at most.

lead.purpose: A stat’s words, a year heading on a person page, a figure in the status strip, the inspector’s state name.

title.purpose: A section heading, in sentence case, with a dot in the page’s hue before it; a state’s name in the inspector’s list; a name in the schedule.

body.purpose: Prose, at 64ch in a sub-line and 78ch in a note.

data.purpose: A table cell, a note under a chart, a row header.

meta.purpose: Captions, the command bar’s text, a number’s unit. Mono and tabular.

label.purpose: A column header, a tab, a rail item, a provenance marker. Never a sentence.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: A section card or the workbench: a lit top edge and a soft ambient drop. An open section has none.

shadows.name: page-glow
shadows.value: radial-gradient(80% 32% at 50% 0, color-mix(in oklab, var(--page) 16%, transparent), transparent 72%)
shadows.purpose: The light along the top of the page, one hue and dim; a seat’s page uses the holding party’s ink.

shadows.name: top-bar-frost
shadows.purpose: The one frosted surface: the sticky top bar.

motion.name: t-1
motion.purpose: A hover or focus change on a control.

motion.name: t-2
motion.purpose: A mark arriving on load, such as a wedge or a bar.

motion.name: t-3
motion.purpose: The longest single animation. 700ms is the ceiling.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The one curve. Everything runs once, on load, inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

components.name: Party Swatch
components.description: A party’s own ink beside its abbreviation. The pair is one mark and never breaks across lines, so identity is never colour alone.

narrative.overview:
The product is a tool for looking at elections, and the interface behaves like the room that tool would live in: dark, quiet, built from a rail of six places, a command bar and a sticky strip across the top, with the data as the only thing that glows. Structure, shape and density do the work. The canvas is a blue-violet black, the chrome is near-black surfaces held to one hue per page, and a party's own colour is the loudest thing a screen can contain because it is the thing the screen is about.

The voice is forensic, instrument-like and civic. Forensic, because every figure carries its source, how it was derived and what is missing, and the surface says so in words: an absence is a phrase, never a bare dash; a derived value is a marked word, never a plain number. Instrument-like, because it is operated: tabs choose a view and the view is URL state, numerals are tabular, labels are small uppercase mono. Civic, because it takes no side: party colours are the parties' own, never the product's, and nothing here recommends, ranks or editorialises.

It rules three looks out, each confirmed. Not a lab report or a school project: flat, all-monospace, hairlines between sections, which this stylesheet used to be and replaced with the card skin. Not TV-news election graphics: saturated party slabs, tickers and hue as decoration. Not a generic SaaS dashboard: glass cards and gradients with nothing behind them. Where the system uses a gradient, a blur or a glow, it is a fixed, bounded device with a stated job, and the data never sits on a decorative one.
keyCharacteristics: Dark only. There is no light surface, and every contrast in the system is measured against the three night surfaces.
Surfaces are neutral near-black. A page shows one signal hue, its own, in a handful of small places; the front page's workbench is its one card, and the reference sections under it are open.
One voice for prose (sans) and one for numbers, marks and metadata (mono, tabular).
Seven spacing steps, seven type sizes, one radius, three inks.
Hue is spent on data first and wayfinding second, and never the other way round. The chrome never shows two signal hues on one page.
Status survives greyscale: a word with a rule under it, never colour alone.
System fonts only; no webfont is loaded.

rules.name: The Data Hue Rule
rules.body: A hue on a data mark means what the data says, and nothing else. A party's colour is the party's, the ramp is a magnitude, the semantic inks are their meaning.

rules.name: The Wayfinding Edge Rule
rules.body: A page shows one signal hue, its own (`--page`, read through `--accent`), and it says where you are, never what a mark is. It appears in five places: the current rail place (a 2px bar and its icon), the 8px marker before a heading, the 2px underline of the selected workbench tab, the kind-of-page label, and one dim glow along the top of the page (16%). It is never cycled by section, never tints a card's edge, wash or foot, never sets type in a gradient, and never fills a seat, a bar, a ribbon, a dot or a legend swatch, because every hue in the band sits within a few ΔE of some party's colour. The other five hues still exist: a kind of page picks one.

rules.name: The Floor Rule
rules.body: Every ink clears 4.5:1 as text on all three night surfaces, and every mark clears 3:1. `iei.test.ts` locks the neutral hexes: do not change one without running it.

rules.name: The Three-Ink Rule
rules.body: There are three reading inks and no fourth. A tier nothing may legitimately use is a tier to delete.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Numbers, marks and metadata are monospace and tabular. Prose is sans. A note under a chart is a sentence and is set as one.

rules.name: The Four Tiers Rule
rules.body: A screen has a title, a metric, body and a label, and they are far enough apart in size that no two look alike. The scale runs 11 to 52px for a reason: when it ran 9.5 to 25, everything had the same visual weight.

rules.name: The Seven Steps Rule
rules.body: Every length is a token. A rule that wants 18px is a rule that hasn't decided whether it means 16 or 24.

rules.name: The Ambient Rule
rules.body: Shadows say what a surface is, never what happened to it. Hover and focus change a border or an ink, and never a shadow.

rules.name: The Bounded Glow Rule
rules.body: Every gradient and blur is a fixed device with a job: the page glow, the card's top highlight, the bar's frost, and the fade that tells a scrolling tab strip there is more. Type is never set in a gradient. A data mark never sits on a decorative one, and alpha is chosen so the dimmest label still clears 4.5:1 under it.

rules.name: The One Radius Rule
rules.body: The corner is 8px everywhere. A new shape that wants a different corner is a new decision, and is made once here.

rules.name: The Word Not Colour Rule
rules.body: Status is a word, a rule style or a shape, never a colour alone: a provenance marker, a party abbreviation beside a swatch, a current-place bar beside a hue, a dashed bar under an unavailable tab.

rules.name: The Once Rule
rules.body: An animation runs once and never loops, and it lasts at most 700ms. It exists only where the motion is the information.

dos: **Do** spend hue on data first: a party's own ink, the margin ramp, a semantic ink for its meaning only.
**Do** give a page one signal hue, its own, in the five places the Wayfinding Edge Rule lists, and no more.
**Do** pair every colour mark with a word, an abbreviation or a shape.
**Do** set numbers in tabular mono and right-align them with their headers; set sentences in sans.
**Do** use only the seven spacing steps and the seven type sizes, and one 8px radius.
**Do** say an absence in words ("not loaded", "not reported"), at a ink that clears 4.5:1.
**Do** run `iei.test.ts` after any change to a neutral hex or a party ink, and `party-ink.test.ts` after any change to the party colours.
**Do** draw a selected-state bar over a rule instead of a border on a corner-less control, so the one-radius rule holds.
donts: **Don't** fill a seat, bar, ribbon, dot or legend swatch with a wayfinding hue.
**Don't** cycle the signal hues by section, tint a card's edge, wash or foot with one, or set a title in a gradient.
**Don't** let a party's colour change with rank, count, page or neighbour.
**Don't** make it a lab report: all-monospace, hairlines between every section, grey 11px captions.
**Don't** make it TV-news graphics: saturated party slabs, tickers, hue as decoration.
**Don't** make it a generic SaaS dashboard: glass cards and gradients with nothing to say.
**Don't** add a fourth ink tier, a second radius, or a length off the seven-step scale.
**Don't** change a shadow on hover or focus, or draw a focus ring that grows the control's box.
**Don't** print an absence as a bare dash, or a derived figure as if it were announced.
**Don't** load a webfont, or loop an animation.
